sourceRender.prompt:
PORTRAIT picture-book COVER in the warm editorial ink-and-wash style of the FIRST reference image. the-plain-door exactly as its reference sheets: single-plain-solid-wood-door-warm-honey-brown; four-recessed-panels-two-small-above-two-tall; leaf-roughly-twice-as-tall-as-wide-standard-door-proportions; round-brass-knob-at-mid-height-on-the-LEFT-edge-as-viewed; no-lettering-no-sign-no-plaque-on-the-door-face-ever; identical-door-design-in-every-state-and-every-era; open-states-show-only-warm-light-through-the-gap-never-what-is-behind; museum-state-frame-plaque-spotlight-rope-sit-beside-or-below-never-on-the-door; nothing-ominous-through-any-gap-warm-light-never-darkness; warm-editorial-register-never-photoreal. THE PLAIN DOOR: a single plain solid-wood door, warm honey-brown, with FOUR recessed panels (two small panels above two tall panels) and a round brass knob at mid-height on the LEFT edge as viewed. Slightly worn, ordinary, well-made. Standard proportions: the leaf roughly twice as tall as wide (about 0.9 m by 2.0 m). The door face NEVER carries lettering, a sign, or a plaque of any kind. The identical door design appears in every state and every era; only its surroundings change. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal. Face-on, door SHUT, set in an ordinary cream plaster wall with a simple wooden casing. The identity of record: four recessed panels (two small above two tall), round brass knob at mid-height on the LEFT edge as viewed, warm honey-brown wood, slightly worn and ordinary. winged-startup exactly as its reference sheets: The startup is a HAND-STACKED tower of two or three flat cream blocks, slightly imperfect and uneven, never a single block and never a neat machine-precise stack.; Cream wings are attached to the tower and the whole reads as LIFT: rising, climbing, or airborne, never sitting still on a surface.; Plate register only: flat solid terracotta ground, a single-weight wobbly confident black ink outline, flat ivory-cream fills as the only fills.; Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, UI, or cursor marks, ever.; Face-on and flat: no perspective, no isometric, no parallelograms, no side faces or edge thickness, no shading, no gradients, no coloured linework.. A low ordinary wall runs across the bottom of the frame with the plain door set into it, shut, warm gold light glowing along the bottom crack and seeping around the leaf edges. Above, vast warm dawn sky fills the frame, and the winged block-tower startup climbs high into it, wings wide, tilted into ascent, trailing two soft paper-warm motion strokes. IGNORE THE SIZE, PLACEMENT AND FLAT TERRACOTTA GROUND OF THE SUPPLIED STARTUP PLATE: here it is airborne, roughly one-fifth of the frame's height, high above the door. The door stays unbranded: no lettering, sign or plaque on the leaf. CRITICAL SAFE MARGINS: the top 10% and bottom 10% of the frame are pure background texture with NO lettering and NO important elements; ALL text and the figure sit inside the central 80% of the frame, because the outer edges will be trimmed. THIS COVER CARRIES 2 LINE(S) OF HAND-LETTERED TEXT AND EVERY ONE IS REQUIRED. Bake them spelled EXACTLY, and NO other text anywhere: "Takeoff Thursdays" | "A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story". COMPOSE THE ART SO THERE IS ROOM FOR THEM: keep an uncluttered, quiet, low-detail area behind every line so each one reads clearly, with the first line(s) toward the top of the frame and the last line small along the bottom. Busy detail, faces, bright highlights and hard edges must not sit under any line of lettering. IF ANY OF THESE LINES IS MISSING FROM THE FINISHED IMAGE THE IMAGE IS WRONG, however good the art is. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, extra words, gibberish lettering, text touching the frame edges, no lettering on the door face, no stray text beyond the title and the universe mark, no logos, no neon, no 3D render.

READABLE SURFACES ARE ORIENTED FOR THEIR READER, NEVER FOR THE CAMERA. Any book, page, letter, card, note, ledger, document, sign or map that a character is reading, writing on or holding belongs to THAT PERSON, so it is oriented to THEM: its TOP EDGE points AWAY from them and its lines run the direction they read. From wherever the camera happens to stand, it is therefore foreshortened, tilted, or partly upside down. NEVER rotate a surface flat and square to the lens so the viewer can read it comfortably. That is the single most common failure on this rule and it reads as staged the instant anyone notices it. IF THE SCENE SPECIFIES EXACT TEXT THAT MUST BE LEGIBLE, SOLVE IT WITH THE CAMERA AND NEVER BY TURNING THE PAGE: move the camera round to the reader's OWN side, over their shoulder or beside their head and looking down as they look down, so the writing is legible AND still correctly oriented for them. Legibility and correct orientation are never in conflict; a page squared up to the lens means the camera was put in the wrong place. Handwriting the scene does NOT specify is abstract handwriting-like line work with no real readable letters. Text the scene DOES specify as an exact quoted string is designed lettering and must be spelled exactly as quoted.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.

note: DERIVATIVE, not a generation. The cover was conformed to the reader platform's page aspect by conform_cover.py. No image model was called and no pixels of the sharp art were repainted; see derivedFrom for the recipe of the render this came from.
